evidence: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:72-73 both call Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...); line 73 has the message 'Null rawTokenId not allowed' but checks grantType. rawTokenId is never checked, so a null would be stored (line 77) and DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId (lines 114-117) would produce '<prefix>:null'. This is a copy-paste bug; the fix is Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...).

DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId (lines ~74-81) requires exactly 6 prefix chars with a fixed 2+2+2 split and throws IllegalArgumentException otherwise. DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit (lines ~70-86) and the lazy paths put gtf.getShortcut() into the maps with no length check. The SPI javadoc at server-spi-private/.../OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:30 even says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut'. All built-in grants use 2 chars (ac, rt, pg, pc, te, cc, ro, ci, dg), but a custom grant that follows the javadoc would encode fine through encodeTokenId and then fail to decode. Add length validation in the factory and fix the javadoc.

DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:106-137. getShortcutByGrantType (lines 110-115) and getGrantTypeByShortcut (lines 125-133) put into grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts without the size-equality duplicate check done in postInit (lines 81-85). A hot-deployed grant whose shortcut collides with an existing one (e.g. 'ac') would overwrite grantsByShortcuts['ac'], so existing authorization_code tokens would decode to the wrong grant. This is real but only happens with runtime-deployed custom grants that have colliding shortcuts, so it is an edge case.

services/src/test/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java:82 catches RuntimeException. The expected failure is IllegalArgumentException, thrown at DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java ~line 93 (unknown grant shortcut 'ac'). An NPE or StringIndexOutOfBounds regression would also make the test pass. testOldToken (line 110) already catches the specific IllegalStateException. Low severity test-precision fix.

testsuite/.../AssertEvents.java isAccessTokenId matcher: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false (no match) when the shortcut DOES match. It should be `!...equals(...)`. The describeTo text 'Not a Token ID with expected grant' confirms the intent is to reject mismatches.

AssertEvents.java isAccessTokenId: the encoding is session(0-1), token type(2-3), grant(4-5), per DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId (substring(4, 6) for gtShortcut). The matcher uses substring(3, 5), which for 'onrtac' gives 'ta'. Combined with the inverted check (issue 4), the comparison never matches, so the matcher only validates the UUID part and never checks the grant type. The comment itself says 'starts at character 4th char' (0-indexed 4). Fix: `!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)`.

server-spi-private/.../OAuth2GrantType.java:102 caches grantType = formParams.getFirst(GRANT_TYPE) in the constructor, and setFormParams (line 105-107) does not update it. So the staleness is possible in principle. However, a repo-wide grep finds no callers of setFormParams (the only Context construction is TokenEndpoint.java:149), and grant_type is not expected to change after dispatch because TokenEndpoint picks the grant provider from it. This is a latent inconsistency, not a current bug. Deriving it in getGrantType() or updating it in setFormParams would be a cheap hardening.
